title: Autoload script with _draw() renders in editor UI after restart (regression in 4.6 beta)
body:
### Tested versions

Godot Version
✅ Affected: Godot 4.6 beta (tested on v4.6.beta1.official [d743736f8])
✅ Not affected: Godot 4.5 stable (works as expected)

### System information

Godot v4.6.beta1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13650HX (20 threads) - 63.62 GiB memory

### Issue description

When an Autoload (singleton) script is decorated with `@tool` and contains a _draw() function (e.g., for custom 2D rendering), its drawn content appears overlaid on the editor UI itself after restarting the editor.

This did not happen in Godot 4.5, where Autoload scripts with `@tool` and _draw() were correctly ignored in the editor viewport unless explicitly added to the scene tree.

The issue seems to be a regression introduced in 4.6 beta, possibly related to changes in how tool-mode singletons are initialized or rendered in the editor context.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a664ec54-0aad-4a2c-ba4d-d1507a383240)




### Steps to reproduce

Steps to Reproduce
1.  Create a new Godot project using Godot 4.6 beta.
2.  Create a GDScript file named TestAutoload.gd with the following content:
   ```gdscript
    @tool
    extends Node2D

    func _draw():
       draw_circle(Vector2(100, 100), 50, Color.RED)
  ```
3. Register it as an Autoload:
    1. Go to Project → Project Settings → Autoload.
    2. Add `TestAutoload.gd` with the name `TestAutoload`
    3. Click `Add`
4. Close the Godot editor completely.
5. Restart the Godot editor and open the project .
6. Observe the editor UI



### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24170538/test.zip)
